headline: Corn slips to $4.58¾ and beans hold $12.53 as WTI tops $101
lead: Corn is at $4.58¾ overnight, down 1¾ cents from Thursday's $4.60½ settle. Beans are flat at $12.53¼, and USDA's October yields are still the supply story. Crude is the mover, up 1.6% to $101.09 as Houthi attacks threaten Saudi energy sites.
teaser: Corn slips to $4.58¾ and beans hold $12.53 as WTI tops $101.

one_number.context: Crude is up 1.6% on Houthi threats to Saudi energy sites. Diesel and fertilizer costs feel that first, well before next spring's input decisions.

sections.title: Grains hold near lows
sections.body:
- Corn is at **$4.58¾** overnight, down 1¾ cents, and wheat is up ¼ cent at $6.25.
- Soybeans are flat at $12.53¼ even though feedstuffs.com says prices are finally noticing Chinese sales.
- Corn and winter wheat slid again Thursday, and harvest supply is still the weight.
sections.so_what: Chinese buying is helping beans, but corn still has harvest pressure.

sections.title: Cattle ease from highs
sections.body:
- Live cattle settled Thursday at **$229.75**, down 0.3%, and feeders fell 0.5% to $346.10.
- AgWeb says cattle hit three-month highs this week, so this is a small give-back.
- USDA plans to reopen the Columbus, N.M., crossing to Mexican cattle Oct. 26, even with two new screwworm cases confirmed.
sections.so_what: Border news adds supply risk to a market near three-month highs.

sections.title: Energy runs higher
sections.body:
- WTI is at **$101.09**, up 1.6%, on Houthi attacks threatening Saudi energy infrastructure.
- Natural gas is up 11.8% to $3.13, and European gas hit its highest level since 2022 as Qatari LNG flows stay restricted.
- USDA put $1.3 billion toward fertilizer manufacturing, a slow fix for input costs.
sections.so_what: Energy costs are rising ahead of next year's input decisions.

outside_the_pit.title: Third border crossing reopens to Mexican cattle Oct. 26
outside_the_pit.body: USDA says Columbus, N.M., reopens Monday, though two new screwworm cases were confirmed last week in the Southwest.

watch_list.desc: Corn back under $4.50 would say harvest supply is still winning.
WTI holding above $100 would keep fuel and fertilizer costs in focus.
Columbus, N.M., crossing reopens to Mexican cattle; new screwworm cases are a risk.

source_summary: CME Group, USDA, ICE, oilprice.com, feedstuffs.com, AgWeb, Farm Policy News

lines: Corn harvest price so far: $4.84 vs $4.62 projected (+4.8%), 16 of 22 trading days in.
Soybeans harvest price so far: $12.75 vs $11.09 projected (+15.0%), 16 of 22 trading days in.
harvest_clock.note: Ours: the average of the daily CBOT settles through Oct 22, figured the way USDA RMA does. RMA posts corn at $4.85 and soybeans at $12.76, both through Oct 21. Window and projected price: USDA RMA, as of Oct 22. Oct 1-31 window, most states.

facts.sentence: On Thursday, Oct 22, 1,729 of the 1,791 elevators AGSIST reads posted a lower cash corn bid than Wednesday, 53 a higher one; 200 changed their basis, 56 weaker and 144 stronger.
facts.detail: 9 unchanged; median change 4¢ lower. Biggest state move: Iowa, 4¢ lower (447 elevators).
facts.unit: cents per bushel, median change in cash bid
facts.source: AGSIST elevator network, last posted bid per trading day (data/bids-prev)

facts.sentence: Corn basis on Oct 23 ran from 55¢ over December futures in Texas to 87¢ under in North Dakota, state medians of the elevators AGSIST read at 5:32 a.m. CT.
